body:
# Independent audit: normal allocation and contact overlap

Source: `candidate 72bbac9873894c0b`, Sections1--5.

Result: PASS. The exact dual is for a fixed actual menu and the stated
erosion family; it is not a selector theorem across menus.

* The two normal-dependent allocation coefficients still sum to one at
  each individual normal. The monotonicity inequality is therefore
  sufficient before integration, and the resulting midpoint inclusion
  is exact. Zero speeds preserve convexity, nesting, and the uniform
  radial bound in the first-variation proof.
* The signed measures include the beta total-cost term and use the
  actual full/proper/empty cap statuses. An outside supporting facet is
  correctly assigned zero loss. Pushforward to normals loses no data
  relevant to this family, because the allocation depends only on n.
* The L2 weak compactness proof gives a compact convex response range.
  Indicator tests preserve 0<=t<=1 and the finite density tests preserve
  every response coordinate. Continuous functions approximate in the
  single dominating finite Radon measure, including its atoms. Clamping
  preserves the required range and improves the approximation error.
* The Hahn-set support formula and finite-dimensional separation give
  exactly the strict positive-orthant criterion. Its separating
  functional must be nonnegative, and compactness of the probability
  simplex supplies the uniform strict margin. No unsupported minimax
  interchange or exact continuous boundary attainment is claimed.
* The contact cutoff is chosen before the shape parameter. On its full
  band the exact one-input proof applies; everywhere else a fixed
  original support gap pays the bounded target speed. Dominated
  convergence, followed by continuous allocation approximation, gives
  the stated overlap infimum. There is no derivative/vanishing-band
  limit interchange.
* Every source cap receives the same ordinary lower payment, whereas
  the proof charges all endpoint cost and discards only nonnegative
  endpoint cap loss. The fixed-cover/slack hypotheses therefore imply
  actual descent under(12). The mutual-singularity corollary uses
  strictly positive bounded weights and is valid. The polytopal
  codimension-two interpretation is correctly scoped and credited.

I independently checked the last numerical normalization: D_K=9,
omega=171/10, beta=800/1803 give source surplus4/601 and beta*omega=4560/601;
the actual input cap loss8 gives additional surplus248/601, hence total
252/601. Thus the source's distinction between exact cap-sensitive
allocation and the weaker cost-only test is substantive.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
